posts.content:
Firefighters seem to have had a pretty good day yesterday- at least on our corner of the fire.  So far they have been very successful holding the fire line and preventing the fire from crossing Wilt Rd and heading up into our neighborhood.  

I watched the back cameras quite alot yesterday and there were fewer smoke events (on Friday there a smoke column would pop up and then go away…). 

At Stevenson we did the hot sauce challenge- you can see Marty bringing the fries and nuggets.  Suz did great filling in for Aaron with Skillethead.  I played the baritone mando part on Dawgs Bull.  4 mandos, 3 fiddles, 2 guitars, dobro!

posts.title: 26July 2026

posts.content:
I didn’t watch the update this morning, but Suz did and I got some info from her.  

There are a bunch more folks and resources on this fire.  They are really throwing everything they have.  Big winds again forecast for today and right at our house.  So far so good.  

They really are working hard to hold that se corner - where we are.  Fingers crossed.  I obsessively watch the cameras and see smoke pop up and go away.

posts.title: 25 July 26

posts.content:
I read that the Akawa fire is now the highest priority fire in the nation.  Not the distinction we want.  Firefighters are pretty much expecting the fire to cross Wilt rd and head into our neighborhood today.  Pretty unnerving and I can’t help staring at our cameras.  Our cameras have shown clear blue skies for the more than the last 12 hours.  It’s 1230 pm and I’m just starting to see some smoke .  Also unnerving.  

The helpless waiting is pretty awful.  Watching the smoke move in on cameras is sort of like trying not to look at a car wreck as you slowly drive by.

posts.title: 24 July26

posts.content:
We still have a house - and power. Our cameras are working and things don’t look terrible this morning on the cameras at home. Nothing in our neighborhood seems to have burned. The watch duty fire perimeter hasn’t updated this morning.  10 hours ago it shows the fire perimeter expanding kind of almost all the way to wilt rd sort of everywhere.  

It rained at home for a while yesterday afternoon.  Here in Stevenson it rained last night and there was 5-6 courtesy thunder booms in the night.

posts.title: 23 July 26

posts.content:
It was a little less Smokey this morning.  We were able to open the windows for a bit.  We left for Stevenson maybe around 930.  

Our neighborhood (sis22) finally went to level 1 around noon today.  We predict we will skip level 2 like last time and go straight to 3.  When that happens is up for debate.  I predict tomorrow at noon.  

Arrived in Stevenson and got mostly set up.  It’s pretty warm here.  

I took a couple creepy photos last night.  The photo with more red blobs shows hot spots- those aren’t in our favor… 

We both are anxious and have that pit in our stomach feeling.  

And we just went to level 2 at 320.  Not looking good.  

And now level 3 at 357….  Here we go.

posts.title: 22July 2026

posts.content:
Technically we are still not even on level 1.   Lots of folks close to our south and west on level 3.  I added some photos from Sunday.  The fire was less defined for the last couple of days.  We have had very little smoke- that all changed today.  

We are worried about Thursday- Saturday.  The wind forecast seems to be strong west winds.  Now that the fire has moved so far south - it’s basically just west of us.  That’s bad- they don’t seem to have any control over it at all. That’s bad too.  

I have that sick feeling again.
